source_text: Si quis dicat: alius est qui passus est, et alius, qui non est passus; et non confitetur, idem impassibile et immutabile Dei Verbum, in carne propria passum immutabiliter, sicut scriptum est; anathema esto. Qua ratione dici potest alius qui passus est, et alius, qui non est passus? cum ipse Dominus dicat: Oportet filium hominis multa pati, et occidi; et die tertia resurgere a mortuis. Et illud: cum videritis filium hominis sedentem in dextera patris, et: cum venerit filius hominis in gloria patris sui.
thought_title: The same Word suffered in his own flesh
orientation: Gregory pronounces condemnation on those who separate a suffering one from one who does not suffer, insisting the same Word suffered in flesh.
pass_a_gloss: If anyone should say: another is he who suffered, and another he who did not suffer; and does not confess the same Word of God incapable of suffering and unchangeable to have suffered in his own flesh without change, as it stands written; let him be anathema. By what reason can it be said another who suffered, and another who did not suffer? since the Lord himself says: It is necessary for the son of man to suffer many things, and to be killed; and on the third day to rise from the dead. And that saying: when you shall see the son of man sitting at the right hand of the father, and: when the son of man shall have come in the glory of his father.

choices.why: keeps the force of inability to suffer stated in the brief for the uncreated
preserves the sameness of root and the adverbial force that the suffering did not change the Word
propria marks the flesh as the Word's own, against reading it as another subject
literal subject title used in the quoted sayings of the Lord

pass_b_english: If anyone says that the one who suffered is one person, and the one who did not suffer is another, and does not confess that the same Word of God, incapable of suffering and unchangeable, suffered without change in his own flesh, as it is written, let him be anathema.

How can it be said that the one who suffered is one, and the one who did not suffer is another? The Lord himself says, "The son of man must suffer many things and be killed, and rise again on the third day" (Luke 9:22). He also says, "When you see the son of man sitting at the right hand of the Father." And, "When the son of man comes in the glory of his Father" (Mark 8:38).
